## Math

The Nernst equation for an electrode potential:

$$
E = E^0 - \frac{RT}{nF}\ln Q
$$ {#eq-nernst}

Refer to it as @eq-nernst. Inline math also works: $i = nFAk^0C$.

## Code

```{python}
#| label: fig-michaelis
#| fig-cap: "Michaelis–Menten response curve"
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
S = np.linspace(0, 10, 200); Vmax, Km = 1.0, 2.0
plt.plot(S, Vmax*S/(Km+S)); plt.xlabel("[S] (mM)"); plt.ylabel("v"); plt.show()
```
